items.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Opens Beijing May 13; Key Meetings Tomorrow-Friday; Iran War Dominant Agenda; Both Sides Signal Compartmentalization; Analyst Consensus: Tariff Truce Over Tehran Commitment
items.summary: President Trump arrived in Beijing on May 12 and the Trump-Xi summit formally opens today (May 13), with key bilateral meetings scheduled for May 14-15. This is Trump's first visit to China since 2017 and his first face-to-face with Xi Jinping since October 2025 — a meeting originally scheduled for early April but postponed due to the Iran war. The Iran war now dominates the summit agenda, with trade, tariffs, Taiwan, and AI as secondary items. China occupies a qualitatively different intermediary position from Pakistan or Qatar: Beijing purchases more than 80% of Iran's shipped crude oil exports, giving it economic leverage over Tehran that no other actor in the current process can match. Chinese exporters, per May 13 CNBC reporting, report that Iran war supply chain disruption concerns now eclipse tariff concerns as their primary operational risk — meaning Xi enters the summit with a domestic economic constituency pressing for Hormuz resolution. These are the conditions under which a Beijing-mediated breakthrough would be structurally plausible. However, analyst consensus projects symbolic output. Reports from PBS and The Columbian cite US and Chinese officials as 'intent on keeping deep differences over Iran war from overshadowing the summit' — a deliberate compartmentalization framing that signals diplomatic management rather than resolution. CSIS, Chatham House, and CFR all project limited near-term Iran breakthroughs; a tariff truce or limited trade framework is the more likely deliverable. The summit's inhibiting effect on Project Freedom resumption is real and structural: it would be diplomatically incoherent to order a strike against Iran while the president is in Beijing with Iran's most significant external partner. That inhibiting window runs approximately 48-72 hours from Trump's arrival through the summit's conclusion. But the inhibiting window is a timing constraint, not a deal advance — the deal track itself is unchanged.

Trump's '1% chance' framing has not been retracted or modified in any presidential statement, Truth Social post, or intermediary communication. The two Axios officials who confirmed Trump's military action lean before the Beijing departure have not been contradicted by any White House or CENTCOM statement. Energy Secretary Wright's 'next few days' military-return timeline (issued May 11 morning) is now in its third day — the Beijing window creates a natural deferral rather than a withdrawal of that signal. The accumulated unanswered CENTCOM incident ledger from the pause remains at 4: the May 9 Saturday naval exchange and the May 11 three-country Gulf drone cluster (UAE, Qatar, Kuwait). CENTCOM has issued no public statement on any of these incidents. New Iran sanctions unveiled May 12 are now operative 24 hours later and unreversed — their operationalization represents an escalation in the coercive pressure track that runs parallel to the nominal pause. The deal track's structural condition entering May 13 morning: Trump '1% chance' unretracted; military lean active; no counter-counter-offer; 4 unanswered kinetic incidents; coercive sanctions escalating; intermediary channels (Pakistan, Qatar) functionally empty. The Beijing window is the only new structural variable preventing an escalation-day designation.

items.headline: Warsh Chair Vote Tomorrow (May 14, 1 Day); Powell Expiry 2 Days (May 15); Reconciliation Finance Text Absent With 2 Days to Deadline; Tariff Truce Expected From Beijing
items.summary: The Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors on May 12 by a 51-45 vote, with only Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) crossing as the sole Democratic crossover. The separate vote to designate Warsh as Fed Chair is expected Wednesday May 14 — 1 day from this brief — ahead of Jerome Powell's 8-year term expiry on Friday May 15. If the chair vote proceeds as scheduled, Warsh will be the nation's 17th Fed Chair effective before Powell's term expires Friday. Warsh's monetary inheritance has not improved since May 12: Brent opened at $107.05 on May 13, and the primary economic shock — Hormuz supply disruption — is immune to interest-rate tools. His first FOMC meeting (expected June 16) will occur either in the aftermath of resumed Project Freedom operations or in the improbable scenario of a Beijing-catalyzed deal reversal. The federal funds rate is currently 3.50-3.75%; the oil shock creates stagflationary pressure that puts Warsh between inflation discipline and growth-recession risk from his first day. Warsh's first public statement as confirmed Chair will be parsed for that positioning. Reconciliation 2.0: the May 15 committee submission deadline is 2 days away. The Senate Finance Committee has not released its tax and revenue provisions text — the most politically volatile and expensive element of the bill. The DHS/Judiciary $72B measure (CBO-scored May 4) is cleared; outstanding committees include Finance, Armed Services, and Health. A Finance deadline miss would be the first concrete evidence that Trump's June 1 completion target is in jeopardy. Trump-Xi summit expected trade output: a tariff truce or limited framework — not structural change — with a tariff truce easing secondary market uncertainty on trade-exposed equities but not offsetting the oil shock.

items.headline: CISA Day 10 Clean: Beijing Window Marginally Inhibits IRGC Pre-Positioning; May 12 Trigger Stack Sustained; Post-Summit Window Is Highest-Risk Period; No Updated Advisory
items.summary: Ten days after Project Freedom launched on May 4, the United States has not sustained a confirmed IRGC-affiliated destructive cyberattack on critical infrastructure. The clean streak is the clearest remaining positive signal in the current environment and enters Day 10 under one new marginal structural improvement: the Beijing summit inhibiting window. The IRGC's cyber retaliation doctrine is most acutely triggered by imminent or actual US kinetic escalation; Trump's physical presence in Beijing for the Trump-Xi summit reduces the near-term probability of a Project Freedom resumption order, which in turn marginally reduces the IRGC's incentive to pre-position cyber capabilities for an immediate retaliatory response. That inhibiting window covers approximately the next 48-72 hours through the summit's conclusion. This is a marginal improvement, not a structural one. The underlying trigger stack from May 12 remains fully intact: (1) Trump's '1% chance' framing eliminates the diplomatic restraint incentive that previously gave IRGC cyber planners a reason to hold back; (2) new Iran sanctions unveiled May 12 are now 24 hours old and operationalize the coercive pressure track — an additional trigger for IRGC escalation doctrine; (3) Wright's 'next few days' timeline signals IRGC planners are operating in a pre-resumption environment; (4) WTI above $100 in supply-crisis pricing removes the oil-market economic restraint incentive. CISA Advisory AA26-097A (April 7) remains operative; no updated emergency directive, FBI/IC3 flash, or sector-specific OT/ICS alert has been issued. CI Fortify (launched May 5) remains active across energy, water, and government facility sectors; FINRA financial-sector alert and NERC grid monitoring remain live. The post-summit window — after Trump returns from Beijing and the military action timeline reactivates — will be the highest-risk IRGC cyber pre-positioning period of the pause if the summit fails to produce a deal-positive signal.

The full BLM OR/WA restriction launch tomorrow is the most operationally significant fire management threshold event of the week absent any red flag or new ignition.

OHA's next case count update is expected Wednesday May 14 (tomorrow); the hospitalization is likely to elevate the update from routine surveillance to a severity-flagged briefing. Active wastewater detections across multiple Oregon counties and the confirmed spread from single-household to multi-household outbreak in Multnomah and Clackamas counties suggest the actual case count is materially higher than 20. Of the published 20 cases, 19 involved unvaccinated individuals or those with unknown vaccination status (95%) — the structural transmission driver. Washington State holds at 40+ confirmed cases year-to-date across 8 counties, with Kittitas County in formal outbreak status. The national CDC confirmed case count stands at 1,842 as of May 7 (6 days stale); 93% of confirmed cases are outbreak-associated across 45 affected jurisdictions. The PNW school-year vaccination catch-up window has narrowed to approximately 2.5 weeks (most PNW school districts close mid-to-late June 2026). Any OHA Wednesday update showing a count materially above 20 would represent the most significant Oregon public health development of the week. A new county-level outbreak declaration or OHA emergency briefing announcement would escalate response urgency with the school year window closing.
